question: Can generic sections at the nonrational j-preimages of a retained curve supply a rational block, or does the quadratic isomorphism sign force every trace to vanish?
inputs: The same 112 retained target/family cells as the completed rational-presentation test. Remove exactly its certified rational linear factors; each remaining monic polynomial has degree 23 or 24. No points or rank labels enter arithmetic.
method: Use full-degree squarefree reductions at odd primes at most 251. Intersect subset sums of irreducible factor degrees to certify irreducibility over Q. For the source-to-target scaling class r=b*A(s)/(a*B(s)), find one irreducible residue factor where r is a unit nonsquare. When both certificates hold, r is nonsquare in the preimage number field and the degree-two isomorphism extension pairs every transported source section with its negative. This excludes rational non-torsion directions in the span of all conjugates of those sections.
checkpointing: Write each completed cell separately. Preserve partial evidence and label a cell UNKNOWN if either certificate is missing. Preserve all completed cells on timeout and mark the rest UNKNOWN. No adaptive extension of primes, families or time cap.
interpretation: A falsifiable exclusion of this explicit simultaneous block constructor. A failure to find a nonsquare witness does not certify a square; an irreducibility failure does not certify a factorization. The theorem is about spans of specialized rational generic sections and their conjugates, not all points over the preimage fields.
